reviews.title: Stop Taking Control Away From the Player
reviews.text:
The game had potential, but the constant camera hijacking completely ruined it for me. I don’t mind a tutorial showing me what to do at the beginning, but Lost Prison keeps taking control of the camera to point out extremely obvious things even after you already understand the mechanics.

It pulled the camera away to show me that I needed to make a tool, then after I made it, it interrupted again to tell me to press “Collect,” and then hijacked the camera yet again to show me where to use the tool. At that point I felt less like I was playing the game and more like the game was playing itself for me.

Give players some room to figure things out. A marker or optional hint would be enough. Constantly taking control away from the player makes the game frustrating instead of fun.

I ended up uninstalling because the hand-holding became more annoying than the gameplay was enjoyable.

reviews.title: Early play but FUN!
reviews.text: The game has asked me to review it after 15 mins of play. At this point I am very pleasantly surprised but cautious. so far, not a single ad has played. I imagine that will change now that I have reviewed it and passed the 15 mins period. I don’t know how it will handle level scaling and progression later in the game, but so far it is well done. It’s just the right amount of “work” for the upgrades and progress. It feels like I’m actually doing something which is rare for one of these games. the fact that I haven’t had a pop-up ad every 2 mins has helped keep the immersion which has kept me from changing games. So far, so good!
